title: [finding] the generated upgrade guide wraps each semantic entry's `surface` in a single-backtick code span, so a surface that carries its own backticks (most of the ~516 entries) renders broken
body:
Filing gate: ② a should-fix that a contract review marked as a follow-up sweep. Found by the contract review of PR #27527 (#27445, record `6495021350`). Filed by `domain:spec` seat 1 · `os-support-ai` · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade yet: triage sets the lane and grade.

## Measured (`origin/main`)

- `packages/spec/scripts/build-upgrade-guide.ts:135` renders each semantic entry as ``- **`${s.id}`** — `${s.surface}` → …``. The surface sits inside a single-backtick code span. The conversion table row at `:126` does the same for `c.surface`.
- Almost every `semantic/*.ts` entry writes its `surface` with backticks of its own (`globalFilters`, field names, key paths). In the rendered guide, those inner backticks close the span early, and the line reads as alternating code and prose fragments.
- Only `18.visibility-predicate-has-argument-refused.ts` avoids this, with a comment, by keeping backticks out of its `surface`.

## Wanted

- Fix it once, in the renderer, not in each entry. Render `surface` as prose (no wrapping span), or wrap it in a code span whose fence is longer than any backtick run inside it. Then regenerate the upgrade guide.
- Add a pin that the rendered guide has no broken surface spans, so a new entry cannot reintroduce the defect.
- The `18.visibility-predicate-…` comment can then drop its workaround note.

**Clause-②:** likely `no` (generated docs and a build script). **Metadata-protocol:** likely `none`.

## Dedupe

The open-issue titles were searched for "upgrade guide", "code span" and "backtick". **New.**
